messages.cli.answer.arg.answer: Your answer to the character's question, in quotes.
messages.cli.answer.empty: Give an answer: elvaria answer <quest> "<your answer>".
messages.cli.answer.refused: Quest {id} is «{status}»: only a quest waiting for your answer can be answered.
messages.cli.answer.summary: Answer the question of a quest waiting for you (elvaria quest show prints it): its assignee goes on with your answer (answer command).
messages.cli.character.add.arg.id: Character id: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. thorn.
messages.cli.character.add.option.level: Starting level 1–10, by how strong the model is (default from the model: Opus or Astra 5, Sonnet, Pro or Sol 4, Argon or Terra 3, Haiku, Flash or Luna 2, any other 1).
messages.cli.character.add.option.model: CLI model (default: the class's suggested model in its own tribe).
messages.cli.character.add.option.name: Display name, up to 24 characters (default: the id, capitalised).
messages.cli.character.add.option.tribe: Tribe, an id in kingdom.tribes (default: the class's suggested tribe).
messages.cli.character.add.summary: Summon a character: class, tribe, model and starting level.
messages.cli.character.bad_id: Character id «{id}» is not valid: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 32 characters, not user, machine or temple.
messages.cli.character.bad_level: The level must be a whole number from 1 to {max}.
messages.cli.character.bad_model: Model «{model}» is not valid: lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens only.
messages.cli.character.exists: Character {id} already exists; summoning never overwrites a character.
messages.cli.character.level.sent: Sent the command to set {character} from level {from} to level {level}: the Steward then gives it quests up to rank {ceiling}.
messages.cli.character.level.summary: Set a character's level, up or down: its next claims go by the new level's rank ceiling (set_level command).
messages.cli.character.level_above_model: Level {level} is above the starting level of model {model} ({suggested}): the Steward takes a level as the model's strength, so it gives this character quests up to rank {ceiling}. If the model is not that strong, lower it: elvaria character level {id} {suggested}.
messages.cli.character.level_from_model: Starting level {level}, from model {model}: the Steward gives it quests up to rank {ceiling}.
messages.cli.character.level_unknown_model: No starting level is known for model {model}: level 1, given rank F quests only. Summon with --level 1–10, by how strong the model is, to start higher.
messages.cli.character.model.arg.model: New CLI model of the same tribe, e.g. gemini-3.8-flash-high.
messages.cli.character.model.invalid_model: Model «{model}» is not valid: lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens only.
messages.cli.character.model.model_not_of_tribe: Tribe {tribe} does not run model {model}: a character's tribe is fixed for life. Summon a character of another tribe instead: elvaria character add
messages.cli.character.model.pool_off: Note: pool {pool} of tribe {tribe}, where {model} runs, is turned off in kingdom.json: the character takes no work until it is on.
messages.cli.character.model.sent: Sent the command to move {character} from {from} to {model}: its next session runs it, and that model's mana gauges bind it. Its level stays {level} (elvaria character level changes it).
messages.cli.character.model.summary: Move a character to another model of its own tribe: its next session runs it, and that model's mana gauges bind it (set_model command).
messages.cli.character.need_model: Tribe {tribe} has no default model for this class; add --model <model>.
messages.cli.character.none: No characters yet. Summon one with: elvaria character add <id> --class <class>
messages.cli.character.release.not_suspended: {character} is «{status}», not suspended: there is nothing to release.
messages.cli.character.release.sent: Sent the command to release {character}: it takes work again.
messages.cli.character.release.summary: Release a suspended character: it is idle again and takes work (release command).
messages.cli.character.suspend.already: {character} is suspended already; elvaria character release {character} brings it back.
messages.cli.character.suspend.holds_quest: Quest {quest} goes on without it (see elvaria quest show {quest}); elvaria quest reassign {quest} gives it to someone else.
messages.cli.character.suspend.holds_review: The Steward stops its review of quest {quest}; the next judge takes it.
messages.cli.character.suspend.option.reason: Why it is suspended (kept with the command).
messages.cli.character.suspend.sent: Sent the command to suspend {character}: it takes no work until elvaria character release {character}.
messages.cli.character.suspend.summary: Suspend a character: it takes no work and lets go of the quest it holds, which goes on without it (suspend command).
messages.cli.character.tribe_disabled: Note: tribe {tribe} is disabled; the character takes no work until the tribe is enabled.
messages.cli.character.unknown: There is no character {character}. See: elvaria character list
messages.cli.column.name: Name
messages.cli.column.title: Title
messages.cli.digest.summary: Print the digest as it stands: everything that waits for you, in two groups (must decide for the work to go on, can wait), each with advice and a command. Reads the kingdom only, spends no mana.
messages.cli.digest.title: Digest {day} · {kingdom}
messages.cli.digest.counts: {must} to decide for the work to go on, {can_wait} that can wait.
messages.cli.digest.group.must: Decide for the work to go on
messages.cli.digest.item.question: Quest {quest} «{title}» asks: {question}.
messages.cli.digest.item.awaiting_seal: Quest {quest} «{title}» (rank {rank}) waits for the royal seal.
messages.cli.digest.item.judge_mana: Quest {quest} «{title}» waits in review, but every judge who may take it is out of mana ({gauges}).
messages.cli.digest.item.unjudgeable: Quest {quest} «{title}» waits in review, but the kingdom has nobody who may judge it.
messages.cli.digest.item.unclaimable: Quest {quest} «{title}» (rank {rank}) is one nobody can take.
messages.cli.digest.item.scope_held: Quest {quest} «{title}» is done but still holds its scope; {waiting} wait for it.
messages.cli.digest.item.draft: Draft quest {quest} «{title}» waits for your confirmation.
messages.cli.digest.item.memo: Memo {memo} ({memo_kind}) from {from}, of quest {quest}, waits for your decision.
messages.cli.digest.item.memo_escalated: Letter {memo} ({memo_kind}) from {from}, of quest {quest}: the Chancellor advises: {triage}; it is yours to decide because {holds}.
messages.cli.digest.item.objection: Objection {memo} from {from}, of quest {quest}: no second judge may read it.
messages.cli.digest.item.mana_asleep: Pool {pool} of tribe {tribe} is out of mana (reset: {resets_at}).
messages.cli.digest.advice.answer: Answer, and the doer goes on.
messages.cli.digest.advice.seal_or_return: Read the work, then seal it, or return it with a note (elvaria return).
messages.cli.digest.advice.retry_or_archive: Read why (elvaria quest show), then retry it, or archive it if you drop it.
messages.cli.digest.advice.judge_other_pool_or_wa: Wait for the reset, or summon a judge of another model on another mana pool.
messages.cli.digest.advice.summon_judge: Summon a judge on a model nobody who worked the quest used.
messages.cli.digest.advice.see_why: Read why (elvaria quest show), then summon or level up a character, or edit the quest.
messages.cli.digest.advice.merge_and_archive: Merge its branch, then archive it: the quests that wait for its scope start.
messages.cli.digest.advice.confirm_or_cancel: Confirm it to open it, or cancel it (elvaria quest cancel).
messages.cli.digest.advice.decide_memo: Read the memo, then decide it once (elvaria memo decide).
messages.cli.digest.advice.weigh_triage: Read the letter and the Chancellor's advice, then decide it once (elvaria memo decide), or confirm the draft it names.
messages.cli.digest.advice.settle_objection: Read the objection and the verdict it contests, then decide it once (elvaria memo decide); edit or reassign the quest if the dispute stands.
messages.cli.digest.advice.wait_or_wake: The Steward probes again after the reset; if you just signed in again, wake it now.
messages.cli.digest.advice.watch_mana: Nothing to do yet; elvaria doctor shows the mana gauges.
messages.cli.digest.live_note: Built now from the files and the event log. Quests waiting for a judge are in the digest the Steward writes to digest/ only.
messages.cli.doctor.adapter_doctor_failed: Tribe {tribe}: the adapter file cannot find or run its CLI: {detail}
messages.cli.doctor.adapter_file_broken: Tribe {tribe}: the adapter file {adapter} does not load, or what it builds does not keep the contract:
messages.cli.doctor.acknowledge_disabled: --acknowledge-terms {tribe}: tribe {tribe} is disabled, so doctor skips it and would record nothing. Enable it in the same command: elvaria doctor --enable {tribe} --acknowledge-terms {tribe}
messages.cli.doctor.auth_not_declared: Tribe {tribe}: adapter {adapter} runs with {declared}, not {auth}. Set tribes[].tool.auth in kingdom.json to one of them.
messages.cli.doctor.command_shell_syntax: Territory {id}: these commands hold shell syntax (a pipe, &&, $VAR, a redirection, an unclosed quote); the Steward runs commands without a shell, so they cannot start:
messages.cli.doctor.enable_adapter_file: --enable {tribe}: the adapter of tribe {tribe} is a file of yours ({adapter}) that has passed no conformance suite yet. Run elvaria tribe check {tribe}: it runs the suite and enables the tribe once it passes.
messages.cli.doctor.docker_down: Docker is not running (docker info does not answer) and territories {ids} have commands that use docker: open Docker Desktop (or start the daemon) before elvaria run. With Docker off, resets and e2e checks fail on the environment: the Steward opens no judge and demotes nobody, but runs them again every {minutes} minutes until Docker is up.
messages.cli.doctor.docker_missing: The docker program is not on PATH, and territories {ids} have commands that use docker.
messages.cli.doctor.docker_up: Docker is running (server {version}); territories {ids} have commands that use docker.
messages.cli.doctor.git_identity_hint: Set one: git -C "{path}" config user.name "<name>" and git -C "{path}" config user.email "<email>" (add --global for every repo).
messages.cli.doctor.git_identity_missing: Territory {id}: git has no user.email in the repo {path}, so the Steward's commits (the submit, a half-done piece kept) will fail and the quest goes to the infirmary with the commit trip.
messages.cli.doctor.git_missing: git was not found on PATH.
messages.cli.doctor.one_pool_judges: Doers on the model {model} have judges of another model on one mana pool only (pool {pool} of tribe {tribe}: {judges}): when that pool closes, or they are suspended, work from that model has nobody to judge it. Add a judge of another model on another mana pool, best on another account.
messages.cli.doctor.login_failed: its adapter says the CLI cannot sign in, without saying why.
messages.cli.doctor.option.acknowledge: Record that you have read and accept the provider's terms for this tribe (ADR 0018).
messages.cli.doctor.option.enable: Check a disabled tribe like every enabled one and turn it on in kingdom.json (enabled: true) only when nothing is wrong with it. A tribe whose adapter is a file of yours is enabled by elvaria tribe check instead.
messages.cli.doctor.option.pin: Pin the CLI version and path just found when they differ from the pinned ones.
messages.cli.doctor.option.tool: Path to a tribe's CLI when it is not on PATH, e.g. claude=C:/…/claude.exe; repeat for several tribes.
messages.cli.doctor.pin_hint: Compare with docs/reference/cli-facts-*.md, then run: elvaria doctor --pin
messages.cli.doctor.powershell: Tribe {tribe}: PowerShell runs local scripts (Execution Policy {policy}), so pnpm.ps1 and npm's other shims start in its sessions.
messages.cli.doctor.powershell_hint: In PowerShell run: Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned (local scripts run, downloaded ones need a signature). A policy set by Group Policy is for the machine's admin to change.
messages.cli.doctor.powershell_missing: Tribe {tribe}: powershell.exe was not found on PATH, so whether it runs scripts (pnpm.ps1) was not checked.
messages.cli.doctor.powershell_refuses: Tribe {tribe}: PowerShell refuses scripts (Execution Policy {policy}). Its sessions run commands in powershell.exe, where pnpm is pnpm.ps1: every pnpm command fails, and a judge cannot run the tests it should try.
messages.cli.doctor.powershell_unread: Tribe {tribe}: PowerShell did not say its Execution Policy (Get-ExecutionPolicy), so whether it runs scripts (pnpm.ps1) was not checked.
messages.cli.doctor.program_hint: doctor looks on the PATH of the shell it runs in, as elvaria run does: add the program's folder to PATH where elvaria run starts (Git for Windows keeps sh in C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin), or change the command.
messages.cli.doctor.program_missing: Territory {id}: {program} is not on PATH, so these commands cannot start:
messages.cli.doctor.program_shell_only: Territory {id}: {program} is {path}, which only a shell can start (a .cmd or .bat that does not run a Node script), so these commands cannot start:
messages.cli.doctor.programs: Territory {id}: the programs of its {count} commands are on PATH ({programs}).
messages.cli.doctor.registry: Registry: {kinds} quest kinds, {classes} classes, {rituals} rituals, {scripts} scripts, {tags} tags.
messages.cli.doctor.registry_behind: The registry lacks {count} entries or fields this Elvaria ships (they came after the kingdom was made):
messages.cli.doctor.registry_behind_hint: elvaria migrate adds the missing entries whole and leaves every entry you have as it is; copy a missing field from {path} by hand if you want it.
messages.cli.doctor.registry_missing: The registry names {count} catalog scripts the kingdom does not have:
messages.cli.doctor.registry_prompts_hint: Run elvaria migrate: it copies the missing class prompts from {path} into registry/prompts/ and leaves the ones you have.
messages.cli.doctor.registry_files_hint: Run elvaria migrate: it copies the registry files this Elvaria ships and the kingdom lacks from {path}, and leaves the ones you have.
messages.cli.doctor.rules_outside_patch: Territory {id}: {count} files under .claude/rules are not in laws.patch_paths; Claude Code cannot write them, so a character has to ask the owner instead of editing. Add "{glob}" to laws.patch_paths in territories/{id}/territory.json:
messages.cli.doctor.rules_patchable: Territory {id}: the {count} files under .claude/rules are all in laws.patch_paths.
messages.cli.doctor.saved: Wrote the tool of tribe {tribes} into kingdom.json.
messages.cli.doctor.shell: Tribe {tribe}: its sessions run commands in {shell}.
messages.cli.doctor.summary: Check that this machine is ready: registry, git, each tribe's CLI (and on Windows whether PowerShell runs scripts, for a tribe whose sessions run commands in it), the territories and the programs their commands start, the treasury, sessions left running.
messages.cli.doctor.terms_refused: Tribe {tribe}: Antigravity's terms are not acknowledged, so this tribe does not run yet (ADR 0018).
messages.cli.doctor.territory_not_git: Territory {id}: {path} is no longer a git repo.
messages.cli.doctor.territory_unchecked: Territory {id}: {path}; its repo cannot be checked without git.
messages.cli.doctor.tool_changed: Tribe {tribe}: found version {version} ({path}), which differs from the pinned {pinned}; keeping the pinned one.
messages.cli.doctor.tool_hint: Show doctor the way: elvaria doctor --tool {tribe}=<path to the CLI>
messages.cli.doctor.tool_moved: Tribe {tribe}: the pinned {pinned_path} is gone; found {path}, version {version}. The tribe cannot run until it is pinned again.
messages.cli.doctor.tool_missing: Tribe {tribe}: {program} was not found on PATH.
messages.cli.doctor.tool_path_bad: Tribe {tribe}: the path given to --tool is not a file ({program}).
messages.cli.doctor.tribe_enabled: Tribe {tribe} is now enabled in kingdom.json.
messages.cli.doctor.tribe_still_disabled: Tribe {tribe} stays disabled until the problem above is fixed.
messages.cli.doctor.tribe_invalid: Tribe {tribe}: its settings are not valid once the tool is filled in:
messages.cli.doctor.unknown_adapter: Tribe {tribe}: there is no built-in adapter {adapter}; a tribe names a built-in adapter or an adapter file adapters/<name>.mjs.
messages.cli.doctor.treasury: Treasury {path}: {count} names, every name the territories allow.
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_absent: Treasury {path}: no file yet; no territory allows a secret.
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_missing_names: Treasury {path} lacks names the territories allow; a quest asking for one goes to the infirmary:

messages.cli.doctor.treasury_not_object: Treasury {path} is not a JSON object of the form { "name": "value" }.
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_bad_name: Treasury {path}: "{name}" is not a secret name (snake_case, like npm_token).
messages.cli.doctor.treasury_bad_value: Treasury {path}: the value of {name} is not a non-empty string.
messages.cli.doctor.sessions_left: {count} sessions a stopped Steward left behind are still running; the next elvaria run kills them:
messages.cli.doctor.session_left_unknown: {quest}: {character} ({role}), pid {pid}: its start time is unknown, so elvaria run leaves it alone; check it by hand and stop it if it is this session
messages.cli.error.bad_value: Option {option} is missing its value, or takes none.
messages.cli.error.locale: There is no language «{value}»; choose one of: {choices}.
messages.cli.error.no_kingdom: No kingdom given: add --kingdom <dir> or set ELVARIA_KINGDOM.
messages.cli.error.not_a_kingdom: {dir} is not a kingdom yet (no kingdom.json). Found one with: elvaria init --kingdom "{dir}" --name <name>
messages.cli.error.time_zone: Time zone «{tz}» is not in the IANA time zone list.
messages.cli.error.unknown: {option} «{value}» does not exist; choose one of: {choices}.
messages.cli.inbox.reason.stale: the quest changed since you read it, so the edit does not overwrite it; read it again with elvaria quest show and send the edit again (an edit that changes only the budget is never refused for this)
messages.cli.inbox.sent: Command {id} is in the inbox; the Steward applies it at its next tick.
messages.cli.inbox.unanswered: A Steward is running but has not answered command {id}: it stays in the inbox (a command that waits for a free character or for mana stays until it can be done); the answer will be a command.applied or command.rejected line in the event log.
messages.cli.init.option.name: Name of the kingdom, up to 24 characters.
messages.cli.init.option.profession: Your profession: developer, ba, marketing, researcher or other (default developer).
messages.cli.init.option.tz: IANA time zone, e.g. Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh (default: the machine's zone).
messages.cli.init.summary: Found a new kingdom: folder, default registry and two tribes.
messages.cli.init.tribes: Tribes: {tribes}. Run elvaria doctor --kingdom "{dir}" to find each tribe's CLI.
messages.cli.mana.asleep: Mana gauge asleep: {gauge}. The characters it binds take no work until the Steward finds the mana back.
messages.cli.mana.asleep_until: Mana gauge asleep: {gauge}, resets at {resets_at}. The characters it binds take no work until the Steward finds the mana back; it probes just after that time.
messages.cli.mana.reading: {window} window: {used_pct}% used, resets at {resets_at} (read at {observed_at}, source {source}).
messages.cli.mana.reading_no_reset: {window} window: {used_pct}% used, reset time unknown (read at {observed_at}, source {source}).
messages.cli.mana.unmeasured: Not measured: the log has no reading of this gauge still in force.
messages.cli.mana.share_measured: One session took up to {pct}% of the {window} window (measured from the log).
messages.cli.mana.share_default: One session's share of the {window} window is not measured yet: the Steward counts {pct}%.
messages.cli.mana.closed_early: Mana gauge closed one session early: {gauge}. Its {window} window is at {used_pct}%, and one more session ({share}%) would take it to {threshold}%: the characters it binds start no new session until it resets; running ones go on.
messages.cli.mana.closed_cap: Mana gauge closed: {gauge}. Its {window} window is at {used_pct}%, at or past {threshold}% (mana.cap_pct and the king's reserve): the characters it binds start no new session until it resets; running ones go on.
messages.cli.mana.none: Mana: not measured; the Steward has logged no reading and no gauge asleep yet (elvaria run reads mana while there is work).
messages.cli.memo.arg.memo: Letter id, e.g. m_20261112_4k2pqz (elvaria memo list prints them).
messages.cli.memo.none_open: No open letters (elvaria memo list --all shows the decided ones too).
messages.cli.memo.list.summary: List the letters characters wrote about work outside their quests (memos), the open ones unless --all.
messages.cli.memo.list.option.all: Also list the letters already decided.
messages.cli.memo.show.summary: Show one letter: who wrote it on which quest, where it went, how it was decided, and its whole text.
messages.cli.memo.show.hint: Decide it: elvaria memo decide {id} shelved (or rejected), or elvaria memo decide {id} handled --quest <quest>; or let the Chancellor draft a quest from it: elvaria say --memo {id}
messages.cli.memo.refusal.no_verdict: its run came back with no fail to contest
messages.cli.memo.refusal.owner_verdict: the verdict is your own return
messages.cli.memo.refusal.final_verdict: the verdict is a second judge's, and final
messages.cli.memo.refusal.second_objection: another objection contests that verdict already
messages.cli.memo.decide.summary: Decide a letter once: set it aside (shelved), refuse it (rejected), or name the quest that does the work (handled --quest); no quest changes (decide_memo command).
messages.cli.memo.decide.option.quest: With handled: the quest that does the work.
messages.cli.memo.decide.option.note: A note kept with the decision.
messages.cli.memo.decide.bad_decision: "{decision}" is no decision: give one of {decisions}.
messages.cli.memo.decide.needs_quest: A handled letter names the quest that does the work: --quest <quest>.
messages.cli.memo.decide.closed: Letter {id} is decided already: a letter is decided once.
messages.cli.metrics.summary: Metrics ledger: runs, rework by cause, first-pass rate, escaped defects, owner interventions. Reads the kingdom only, spends no mana.
messages.cli.metrics.option.since: From this day on, that day included (yyyy-mm-dd).
messages.cli.metrics.option.until: Up to this day, that day included (yyyy-mm-dd).
messages.cli.metrics.option.json: Print the whole ledger as JSON instead of tables.
messages.cli.metrics.bad_day: {option} takes a day as yyyy-mm-dd, not "{value}".
messages.cli.metrics.title.reads: Files a session read again (at most {shown} rows, the most read first)
messages.cli.metrics.title.prompts: Prompt size by role and block (characters)
messages.cli.metrics.line.runs: Runs: {entries} ({sessions} character sessions, {machine} machine runs); {paused} sessions stopped by mana; {sequels} extra sessions inside a run.
messages.cli.metrics.line.escaped: Escaped defects (the owner returned a passed run): {count}.
messages.cli.metrics.line.owner: Owner interventions: {count} commands, on {quests} of {worked} quests.
messages.cli.metrics.line.sealed: Sealed quests: {count}, {tokens} tokens in all, {minutes} minutes on average from first session to last.
messages.cli.metrics.line.set_aside: Check runs set aside for their environment (Docker down, a container gone): {count}.
messages.cli.metrics.line.reads: File reads: {total}; {files} files a session read more than once.
messages.cli.metrics.line.graph: Code graph queries: {total} in {sessions} sessions (query {query}, path {path}, explain {explain}, affected {affected}).
messages.cli.metrics.line.first_edits: Assignee sessions: {sessions}, {edited} edited a file; before the first edit: {median} tool calls at the median, {share} of all their calls ({median_share} at the median).
messages.cli.metrics.line.out_of_scope: Submits that changed files outside their quest's scope: {count} ({files} files).
messages.cli.metrics.cause.question: question
messages.cli.metrics.limit.rule: Rework is every character session beyond one assignee and one verifier per quest; sessions stopped by mana and machine runs are not counted.
messages.cli.metrics.limit.check: A check that went red on files Elvaria wrote into the worktree shows as output: the verdict does not say whose file failed.
messages.cli.metrics.limit.crash: A verifier crash covers both a dead CLI and an invalid verdict.
messages.cli.metrics.limit.cancelled: cancelled covers both a release when the Steward restarts and a cancel by the owner.
messages.cli.metrics.limit.day: A timestamp belongs to the day it is written in, in the zone of the kingdom; owner commands are counted by their command.applied line: the kind from the line (since PS-01b) or from inbox/done, the quest from inbox/done.
messages.cli.metrics.limit.set_aside: Checks set aside for their environment are counted only on check.end lines written since PS-01b; before, they show as failed checks.
messages.cli.metrics.limit.reads: A read is an agent.tool line of kind read that names a path; a line with no session counts in the total only. Lines written before PS-21 still count Glob, Grep and LS (agy: grep_search, find_by_name, list_dir) as reads; since PS-21 they are searches.
messages.cli.metrics.limit.first_edits: Calls before the first edit count the agent.tool lines of each assignee session, the apprentice's included; the role comes from the attempt log, so the extra sessions inside a run, which it does not name, are left out.
messages.cli.metrics.limit.prompts: Prompt sizes are in characters, trimmed, from the load trace of a session's opening line (since PS-01b); a session that followed the first in a run has none.

messages.cli.build.doctor_here: The kingdom pins build {sha}, but this command runs from {root} (--here).
messages.cli.option.locale: Output language: vi or en (default: the kingdom's language).
messages.cli.quest.add.contract_kind: --contract opens a party: the kind must deliver a list of sub-quests ({kinds}), and not on the script tier.
messages.cli.quest.add.no_blind_trial: Note: a single quest never has a blind trial, though territory {territory} holds one for parties of rank {min_rank} and above. To have one, open the work as a party: --contract (kind {kinds}).
messages.cli.quest.add.option.class: Required class (default: the only class the kind allows).
messages.cli.quest.add.option.contract: The quest is a party's contract quest: its lead writes the contract and the parts, the Steward adds the merge quest. In the description, a line --- ends the work: what follows is for the lead alone, and a blind trial's test writer never reads it.
messages.cli.quest.add.option.depends_on: A quest that must be done first; repeat for several quests.
messages.cli.quest.add.option.kind: Quest kind, from registry/kinds.json (build, fix, document…).
messages.cli.quest.add.option.params: Script parameters, as a JSON object.
messages.cli.quest.add.option.rank: Rank: F, E, D, C, B, A or S.
messages.cli.quest.add.option.scope: A glob of the files the quest changes, relative to the territory root; repeat for several. Two quests whose scopes meet never run at once on one territory; a quest without a scope runs alone there.
messages.cli.quest.add.option.script: Run on the script tier: an id in registry/scripts.json, no model, no mana.
messages.cli.quest.add.option.seal: Needs the royal seal before done (--no-seal to turn off; default from the kind).
messages.cli.quest.add.option.tag: Expertise, from registry/tags.json; repeat for several tags (up to 6).
messages.cli.quest.add.option.title: Title, up to 120 characters.
messages.cli.quest.add.option.to: The character to give it to: only it takes the quest, whatever its level (above its ceiling the quest waits for your seal). Of the quest's class; not for a script-tier quest.
messages.cli.quest.add.sent: Sent the command to create quest «{title}».
messages.cli.quest.add.sent_to: Sent the command to create quest «{title}» for {character}: only {character} takes it.
messages.cli.quest.add.summary: Add a quest that opens at once, without the Chancellor (create_quest command).
messages.cli.quest.add.to_script: --to names who works a session; a script-tier quest (--script) runs without anyone.
messages.cli.quest.assignee.above_ceiling: {character} is level {level} and is given up to rank {ceiling}: this rank {rank} quest waits for your royal seal when done.
messages.cli.quest.assignee.class_mismatch: {character} is a {class}; the quest needs a {required}.
messages.cli.quest.assignee.suspended: {character} is suspended and takes no work.
messages.cli.quest.assignee.tribe_disabled: {character} is of tribe {tribe}, which is disabled: it takes no work until the tribe is enabled.
messages.cli.quest.bad_params: --params must be a JSON object, e.g. {"path": "docs"}.
messages.cli.quest.archive.refused: Quest {id} is «{status}»: only a done quest, or one in the infirmary, can be archived (use elvaria quest cancel for an unfinished one).
messages.cli.quest.archive.sent: Sent the command to archive quest {id}: the Steward removes its worktree and keeps its branch.
messages.cli.quest.archive.summary: Archive a done, delivered quest, or one in the infirmary that the owner gives up: the Steward removes its worktree and keeps its branch (archive command).
messages.cli.quest.archive.undelivered: Quest {id} is not delivered yet: run elvaria run so the Steward delivers it first, then archive it.
messages.cli.quest.cancel.refused: Quest {id} is «{status}»: it can no longer be cancelled.
messages.cli.quest.cancel.sent: Sent the command to cancel quest {id}.
messages.cli.quest.cancel.sent_infirmary: Quest {id} is in the infirmary, where cancelling means archiving: sent the command to archive it; the Steward removes its worktree and keeps its branch with the work done.
messages.cli.quest.cancel.summary: Cancel an unfinished quest; a draft is discarded, and one in the infirmary is archived (cancel or archive command).
messages.cli.quest.confirm.refused: Quest {id} is «{status}»: only a draft needs confirming.
messages.cli.quest.confirm.sent: Sent the command to confirm quest {id}.
messages.cli.quest.confirm.summary: Confirm a draft quest so it opens (confirm command).
messages.cli.quest.edit.bad_number: {option} must be a whole number, not negative (minutes and attempts from 1).
messages.cli.quest.edit.minutes_cut: Warning: the session working quest {id} has run {ran} minutes, past the new {minutes}-minute ceiling: the Steward cuts it at its next tick, as the time breaker does, and the quest goes to the infirmary (elvaria quest show says why; elvaria quest retry opens it again).
messages.cli.quest.edit.minutes_cut_judge: Warning: the judge's session on quest {id} has run {ran} minutes, past the new {minutes}-minute ceiling: the Steward cuts it at its next tick, as the time breaker does; the judge leaves and the next one takes the review, under the new ceiling.
messages.cli.quest.edit.minutes_lowered: Quest {id} has a session running, {ran} minutes so far: the Steward's time breaker reads the quest's ceiling on every tick, so this session too is cut at {minutes} minutes (was {was}), not only the next one.
messages.cli.quest.edit.minutes_raised: Quest {id} has a session running, {ran} minutes so far: the Steward's time breaker reads the quest's ceiling on every tick, so from its next tick this session may run up to {minutes} minutes (was {was}), not only the next one. Unless its CLI took its own clock when the session opened (agy, --print-timeout): that one still stops it at {was} minutes, as the time breaker would, and the next session has the new ceiling.
messages.cli.quest.edit.nothing: Nothing to change: add at least one option (--title, --rank, --seal…).
messages.cli.quest.edit.option.depends_on: The new list of dependencies, replacing the old one; repeat for several quests.
messages.cli.quest.edit.option.scope: The new scope, replacing the old one: a glob of the files the quest changes; repeat for several.
messages.cli.quest.edit.option.seal: Require (--seal) or drop (--no-seal) the royal seal.
messages.cli.quest.edit.self_dependency: A quest cannot depend on itself.
messages.cli.quest.edit.sent: Sent the command to edit quest {id}.
messages.cli.quest.edit.summary: Change a quest without touching its file (edit_quest command).
messages.cli.quest.field.question: Question
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.head: In the infirmary: {why}.
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.trip.time: the time breaker stopped the session
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.trip.tokens: the token breaker stopped the session
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.trip.turns: the turn breaker stopped the session
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.trip.commit: the commit was refused, so the branch lacks the work
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.trip.secrets: a secret the quest asks for is missing, so no session can open
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.trip.forbidden_paths: the session left a forbidden path changed in the plot, so nothing was committed
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.trip.no_verdict: its judges left without a verdict
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.trip.partial_verdict: its judges kept handing in partial verdicts
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.trip.script_usage: the script could not use the quest's params
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.trip.script_fail: the script ran but did not pass
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.detail.paths: Changed in the plot, though laws.forbidden_paths forbids them: {paths}. Only a program the session's shell ran could write there (an interpreter such as node, pnpm or npx in the class's tools.allow opens every path to the character's scripts). Put them back or remove them in the plot, then elvaria quest retry.
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.detail.paths_more: Changed in the plot, though laws.forbidden_paths forbids them: {paths} and {count} more (the journal lists them all). Only a program the session's shell ran could write there (an interpreter such as node, pnpm or npx in the class's tools.allow opens every path to the character's scripts). Put them back or remove them in the plot, then elvaria quest retry.
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.detail.wip: The WIP commit was refused too; the work stays in the plot: {why}
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.detail.apprentice_le: An apprentice of the session ran past its minutes or was cut at its turns: open a child quest for the work it left (see handover.md).
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.detail.verifiers_sto: {count} verifiers of this attempt left without a verdict (a breaker stopped them, or their output was none), so no further one opens: raise the budget (elvaria quest edit), or give the review another judge, before a retry.
messages.cli.quest.infirmary.detail.partial_verdi: {count} verifiers of this attempt handed in a partial verdict, so no further one opens: read their notes (elvaria quest show prints them), and make sure the next judge can finish the ritual (run the checks' commands in its shell, name its breaks), before a retry.
messages.cli.quest.list.option.status: Only this status (an id, e.g. open); repeat for several statuses.
messages.cli.quest.list.option.territory: Only the quests of this territory.
messages.cli.quest.list.summary: List the quests on the quest board.
messages.cli.quest.list.waiting: {count} commands wait for the Steward in the inbox.
messages.cli.quest.party.unknown: {party}: the contract quest cannot be read
messages.cli.quest.reassign.option.to: The character to give it to, of the quest's class, whatever its level (above its ceiling the quest waits for your seal). Without it, the Steward picks among the free ones.
messages.cli.quest.reassign.refused: Quest {id} is «{status}»: only an open quest, one paused for mana, a returned one or one in the infirmary can be given to someone, and never a script-tier one.
messages.cli.quest.reassign.sent: Sent the command to give quest {id} to someone else: the Steward picks among the free characters of its class.
messages.cli.quest.reassign.sent_to: Sent the command to give quest {id} to {character}.
messages.cli.quest.reassign.summary: Give a quest to another character, or to the one you name (reassign command).
messages.cli.quest.retry.option.to: The character to work it again, of the quest's class, whatever its level (above its ceiling the quest waits for your seal): only it takes the quest, with its full attempt budget (reassign command). Without it, the quest opens for every free character of its class.
messages.cli.quest.retry.refused: Quest {id} is «{status}»: only a quest in the infirmary can be retried.
messages.cli.quest.retry.sent: Sent the command to open quest {id} again.
messages.cli.quest.retry.sent_open: Sent the command to open quest {id} again, for every free {class}: the Steward gives it to one of them, as any open quest, not necessarily to the one who worked it. To give it to one character: elvaria quest retry {id} --to <character>
messages.cli.quest.retry.sent_review: Sent the command to retry quest {id}: its review goes on with a new judge, in the same run (its judges left without a verdict or only read in part: raise its budget first if the breakers cut them, give it another judge if their output was none, or make sure the next judge can finish the ritual if they handed in partial verdicts).
messages.cli.quest.retry.sent_to: Sent the command to retry quest {id} with {character}: only it takes the quest, with its full attempt budget (reassign command).
messages.cli.quest.retry.summary: Open a quest in the infirmary again with its full attempt budget, for every free character of its class or for the one --to names, or send one whose judges kept leaving without a verdict, or with a partial one, back to review (retry command; reassign with --to).
messages.cli.quest.retry.to_review: Quest {id}'s work is done and only its review stalled: a retry sends it back to review with a new judge, and --to names who works a quest, not who judges it. Retry it without --to; to have {character} do the work again instead: elvaria quest reassign {id} --to {character}
messages.cli.quest.retry.to_script: Quest {id} is script-tier: no character works it, so --to has no one to name. elvaria quest retry {id} runs its script again.
messages.cli.quest.run.head: Attempt {run}:
messages.cli.quest.run.partial: Partial verdict of {who}, read up to: {until}
messages.cli.quest.run.restored: The Steward put the plot back to its commit, dropping {count} path(s) that commands (a judge's or the checks') left there:
messages.cli.quest.run.restored_more: …and {count} more (the quest's journal has them all)
messages.cli.quest.scope.waits_alone: waits for {holder}: a quest without a scope runs alone
messages.cli.quest.scope.waits_scope: waits for {holder}, whose scope meets its own
messages.cli.quest.too_many_tags: A quest has at most {max} tags.
messages.cli.quest.unclaimable.hint: {count} quests nobody can take; see why: elvaria quest show <id>.
messages.cli.quest.unclaimable.level_too_low: Nobody can take rank {rank}: the highest {class} is {character} at level {level}, who takes up to {ceiling} ({stretch} when nobody else can).
messages.cli.quest.unclaimable.no_class: No {class} can take it: suspended characters and disabled tribes do not count.
messages.cli.quest.unclaimable.party_bars: Its party bars every {class} there is: each one judged a quest of the party, or worked the other side of its blind trial.
messages.cli.quest.unclaimable.reassign: Give it to {character} (waits for your seal): {command}
messages.cli.quest.unclaimable.reassign_barred: Give it to one of them anyway (your reassign is not barred; the party loses that separation): {command}
messages.cli.quest.unknown_territory: There is no territory {id}. See: elvaria territory list
messages.cli.return.bad_fail_kind: --fail-kind {given} is not a kind of failure; use one of: {kinds}.
messages.cli.return.note_too_short: A return needs a specific note of at least {min} characters (--note): what is wrong and where.
messages.cli.return.option.fail_kind: What kind of failure, so the same failure in a row is counted: tests_fail, scope_creep, missing_i18n, wrong_facts, incomplete, style, unsafe or other (default).
messages.cli.return.option.note: What is wrong and where, at least 20 characters: the assignee reads it in its next session.
messages.cli.return.option.rejudge: The judge erred, not the assignee (it broke nothing, its shell could not run the tests): the work goes back for a new judgement, and the return counts in neither the assignee's reputation nor its fail streak.
messages.cli.return.refused: Quest {id} is «{status}»: only work waiting for your seal can be returned.
messages.cli.return.sent: Sent the command to return quest {id} to its assignee.
messages.cli.return.sent_rejudge: Sent the command to return quest {id} for a new judgement; its assignee is not charged with a fail.
messages.cli.return.summary: Return work waiting for your seal to its assignee, with a note (return command; weighs three verdicts).
messages.cli.run.locked: Another Steward is already running in {kingdom}: one kingdom has one Steward.
messages.cli.run.notice.awaiting_seal: Quest {quest} «{title}» passed review and waits for your seal.
messages.cli.run.notice.environment: Quest {quest} «{title}» waits in review: its check {check} failed because of its environment, not the work ({line}). No judge reads it and nobody loses a level; the checks run again in {minutes} minutes. Log: {log}
messages.cli.run.notice.mana_asleep: Out of mana: {gauge}. What runs on it pauses and keeps its character; the Steward probes until the mana is back.
messages.cli.run.notice.mana_asleep_until: Out of mana: {gauge}, until {resets_at}. What runs on it pauses and keeps its character; the Steward probes just after the reset.
messages.cli.run.notice.mana_awake: Mana is back: {gauge}. Its paused quests go on.
messages.cli.run.notice.mana_warning: Mana running low: {gauge} has used {used_pct}% of its {window} window. Near the cap the world stops taking work there; elvaria character model moves a character to another model.
messages.cli.run.build_source: Running from the source at {root}, not from a pinned build.
messages.cli.run.notice.question: Quest {quest} «{title}» asks you: {question} To answer: elvaria answer {quest} "…"
messages.cli.run.notice.subquests_refused: Plan {quest} «{title}» is delivered but opened no sub-quest: {reason}. See: elvaria quest show {quest}
messages.cli.run.notice.suspended: {character} failed the same way ({fail_kind}) {count} times in a row and went to the Temple.
messages.cli.run.notice.unclaimable: Quest {quest} «{title}», rank {rank}, waits. {reason} See: elvaria quest show {quest}
messages.cli.run.notice.judge_mana: Quest {quest} «{title}» waits in review, but every {classes} who may judge it is out of mana: {gauges}. The review opens once a pool opens again; not to wait, summon a judge of another model on another pool: elvaria character add <id> --class {class} --tribe <tribe>
messages.cli.run.notice.digest: Digest {day}: {must} to decide for the work to go on, {can_wait} that can wait. Read it in {file}.
messages.cli.run.notice.unjudgeable: Quest {quest} «{title}» waits in review, but no {classes} of the kingdom may judge it: the judge must not have worked on it and must run another model than {model}. Summon one: elvaria character add <id> --class {class} --model <model>
messages.cli.run.started: The Steward is running in {kingdom}, one tick every {seconds} s. Ctrl+C stops it.
messages.cli.run.stopping: Stopping the Steward: the sessions it runs end, and their quests are taken up again at the next start.
messages.cli.run.summary: Run the Steward: it gives quests to characters and has their work judged, until you stop it (Ctrl+C).
messages.cli.run.tribe_idle: Tribe {tribe}: adapter {adapter} has no runner yet, so this tribe takes no quest.
messages.cli.run.tribe_broken: Tribe {tribe}: adapter file {adapter} does not load, so this tribe takes no quest:
messages.cli.sandbox.bad_date: --date must be a real date as YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-11-06.
messages.cli.sandbox.bad_line: The line at byte {offset} is skipped ({code}): {message}
messages.cli.sandbox.bad_seed: --seed must be a whole number from 0 to {max}.
messages.cli.sandbox.bad_speed: --speed must be a number above 0, e.g. 20.
messages.cli.sandbox.empty: {file} has no line that can be read.
messages.cli.sandbox.generate.option.date: The fake date, YYYY-MM-DD in the kingdom's time zone (default: today).
messages.cli.sandbox.generate.option.day: Scenario: busy, quiet or mana-out (default busy).
messages.cli.sandbox.generate.option.seed: A whole number from 0; the same seed gives the same day (default: random, printed so it can be repeated).
messages.cli.sandbox.generate.summary: Generate a fake day into the kingdom's events/sandbox/ (the sandbox): no session runs, no real quest is touched.
messages.cli.sandbox.generated: Generated the fake day «{day}» (seed {seed}) for {date}: {lines} lines, {quests} quests, {characters} characters.
messages.cli.sandbox.line.character.sleep: {name} sleeps: tribe {tribe} is out of mana
messages.cli.sandbox.line.command.applied: The Steward applies a command from the inbox
messages.cli.sandbox.line.command.rejected: The Steward refuses a command from the inbox
messages.cli.sandbox.line.mana.exhausted: Tribe {tribe} is out of mana ({pool}): the whole tribe sleeps
messages.cli.sandbox.line.mana.probe: The Steward probes the mana of tribe {tribe}
messages.cli.sandbox.line.quest.created: {quest} «{title}» is on the quest board: {kind}, rank {rank}
messages.cli.sandbox.line.quest.paused: {quest} pauses: the tribe of {assignee} is out of mana
messages.cli.sandbox.line.quest.released: {quest} «{title}» goes back to the quest board
messages.cli.sandbox.line.quest.resumed: {assignee} goes on with {quest} in a fresh session
messages.cli.sandbox.line.quest.verdict: {quest} passes and waits for the royal seal
messages.cli.sandbox.no_file: There is no file {file}. Generate a day with: elvaria sandbox generate --day busy
messages.cli.sandbox.problem.missing_entry: The scenario needs the {what} «{id}» in the kingdom's registry.
messages.cli.sandbox.problem.missing_tribe: The scenario needs tribe {tribe} in kingdom.tribes (elvaria init writes claude and gemini).
messages.cli.sandbox.problem.not_allowed: The registry does not let the kind {kind} use {id}, which the scenario needs.
messages.cli.sandbox.replay.end: ── end of the fake day: {lines} lines ──
messages.cli.sandbox.replay.end_issues: ── end of the fake day: {lines} lines, {issues} unreadable ──
messages.cli.sandbox.replay.option.speed: How many times faster than real time (default 20: ten hours in thirty minutes).
messages.cli.sandbox.replay.option.to: Where to play it: terminal (the herald streams it over the WebSocket from stage 2).
messages.cli.sandbox.replay.summary: Replay a fake day as a timeline in the terminal.
messages.cli.say.answer_hint: To answer, speak again with the answer in your words (elvaria say "…"), then drop the old draft: elvaria quest cancel <id>.
messages.cli.say.arg.words: What you want done, in your own words, in quotes; with --memo, optional.
messages.cli.say.confirm_hint: Once the Steward has applied the commands (elvaria run), confirm each draft so it opens: elvaria quest confirm {id}
messages.cli.say.drop.class_not_allowed: class {detail} does not take this kind
messages.cli.say.drop.dependency_cycle: it waits on drafts that wait on it
messages.cli.say.drop.invalid_script_params: the script's params do not fit its catalog entry ({detail})
messages.cli.say.drop.needs_dropped_draft: it needs draft {detail}, which was dropped
messages.cli.say.drop.over_context_budget: it is too long for one session (estimated tokens {detail}) and was not split; ask again, or ask for a plan
messages.cli.say.drop.party_part: only the party lead splits a party into parts
messages.cli.say.drop.script_not_for_kind: script {detail} does not do this kind
messages.cli.say.drop.secret_not_allowed: the territory does not allow secret {detail}
messages.cli.say.empty: Say something: elvaria say "<what you want done>", or hand over a letter: elvaria say --memo <memo>.
messages.cli.say.failed.invalid_reply: The Chancellor's reply does not follow the {contract} contract:
messages.cli.say.failed.stopped: The Steward stopped while the Chancellor was answering; the session was ended.
messages.cli.say.failed.no_reply: The Chancellor's session ended without a reply (outcome {outcome}).
messages.cli.say.failed.rate_limited: The Chancellor's tribe has run out of mana for now; try again when it is back.
messages.cli.say.failed.timed_out: The Chancellor did not answer in time; the session was stopped.
messages.cli.say.no_chancellor: Nobody can speak as the Chancellor: summon an idle character of class {class} in a tribe that runs, e.g. elvaria character add aldric --class {class} --tribe claude.
messages.cli.say.option.memo: Hand the Chancellor a letter (memo) instead of, or along with, your words: it drafts quests from it.
messages.cli.say.memo_words: A letter ({kind}) that {from} wrote while working on quest {quest}: {body} Files: {refs}.
messages.cli.say.memo_hint: The drafts carry letter {memo}: confirming one of them closes the letter as handled by that quest (elvaria quest confirm <id>).
messages.cli.say.nothing: No draft is left to send.
messages.cli.say.question: The Chancellor asks: {question}
messages.cli.say.run_dir: The prompt and the session's output are in {dir}.
messages.cli.say.summary: Tell the Chancellor what you want: it drafts the quests, you confirm them (create_quest commands, draft).
messages.cli.seal.option.note: A word for the assignee, kept with the seal.
messages.cli.seal.refused: Quest {id} is «{status}»: only work waiting for your seal can be sealed.
messages.cli.seal.sent: Sent the command to seal quest {id}.
messages.cli.seal.summary: Seal work waiting for your seal: the quest is done (seal command; weighs three verdicts).
messages.cli.territory.add.option.branch: Default branch, where quest branches start (default: origin's HEAD, then the branch checked out).
messages.cli.territory.add.option.id: Territory id (default: the folder name, lowercase, joined by hyphens).
messages.cli.territory.add.option.kind: Territory kind: code, docs, content, data or mixed (default code).
messages.cli.territory.add.option.name: Display name, up to 24 characters (default: the folder name).
messages.cli.territory.add.summary: Attach a repo or folder to the kingdom (open a realm).
messages.cli.territory.bad_id: Territory id «{id}» is not valid: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 32 characters, not global; set one with --id.
messages.cli.territory.git_missing: The folder has .git but git was not found on PATH.
messages.cli.territory.id_taken: Territory {id} already exists; choose another id with --id.
messages.cli.territory.inside_repo: Note: the folder is inside the git repo {root}; quest branches will start from that repo.
messages.cli.triage.summary: The Chancellor triages the letters sent to it that wait: one model call for the batch (at most 20, the oldest first). Within kingdom.delegation the Steward applies its decisions without you; the others come to you with its advice, in the digest. kingdom.schedule.triage runs it each day before the digest.
messages.cli.triage.none: No letter waits for the Chancellor.
messages.cli.triage.more: {count} more letters wait for the next triage.
messages.cli.triage.sent: {count} commands sent to the Steward; a running Steward applies them at its next tick. What is left for you: elvaria digest
messages.cli.triage.done: Triage of {count} letters: {delegated} decided without you, {escalated} sent up to you.
messages.cli.triage.hold.mana_over_budget: it costs more mana than its rank
messages.cli.triage.hold.above_rank: the work's rank is above the delegation
messages.cli.triage.hold.outside_scope: its files lie outside the work's scope
messages.cli.triage.hold.chancellor_asks: the Chancellor sends it to you
messages.cli.tribe.add.arg.id: The new tribe's id, e.g. codex: lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter.
messages.cli.tribe.add.bad_adapter: There is no built-in adapter {adapter}. Built in: {adapters}; or an adapter file adapters/<name>.mjs in the kingdom.
messages.cli.tribe.add.bad_id: {id} is not a tribe id: lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter.
messages.cli.tribe.add.bad_tribe: Tribe {id}: --adapter {adapter} or --max-concurrent {max} is not valid. An adapter is a built-in name or adapters/<name>.mjs; max-concurrent is a whole number from 1.
messages.cli.tribe.add.exists: The kingdom already has a tribe {tribe}.
messages.cli.tribe.add.next: Next: elvaria doctor --tool {tribe}=<path to its CLI> pins the CLI, then elvaria tribe check {tribe} runs the conformance suite and enables the tribe once it passes.
messages.cli.tribe.add.no_file: Adapter {adapter}: {file} does not exist. Put the adapter file there first.
messages.cli.tribe.add.option.adapter: claude_code, antigravity, gemini_cli, codex_cli, or adapters/<name>.mjs: a file you put in the kingdom's adapters folder that exports createAdapter(kit).
messages.cli.tribe.add.option.max_concurrent: Sessions the account runs at once (default 1).
messages.cli.tribe.add.summary: Add a tribe: an adapter (built in, or a file adapters/<name>.mjs in the kingdom) and your own account. It starts disabled; existing characters do not change.
messages.cli.tribe.check.broken: Tribe {tribe}: adapter file {adapter} does not load, or what it builds does not keep the contract:
messages.cli.tribe.check.enabled: Tribe {tribe} passes the conformance suite and is now enabled in kingdom.json.
messages.cli.tribe.check.failed: Tribe {tribe} does not pass, so it stays disabled.
messages.cli.tribe.check.failed_enabled: Tribe {tribe} does not pass. It is still enabled; elvaria tribe disable {tribe} stops it taking new work.
messages.cli.tribe.check.left_workspace: ! {check}: the check's temp folder would not go ({problem}): a process of the CLI still holds it. The check does not fail for that; remove the folder once the CLI is done with it: {dir}
messages.cli.tribe.check.max_rank: It takes quests of rank F to {rank}.
messages.cli.tribe.check.no_guarded: Without a tool gate it takes no quest on a territory with read_before_write or rank_floor laws.
messages.cli.tribe.check.no_shell: It declares no shell, so its prompt names none.
messages.cli.tribe.check.no_runner: Tribe {tribe}: adapter {adapter} has no runner yet, so there is nothing to check.
messages.cli.tribe.check.not_pinned: Tribe {tribe} passes, but its CLI is not pinned yet, so it stays disabled: run elvaria doctor --tool {tribe}=<path to its CLI>, then check again.
messages.cli.tribe.check.option.model: Model of the probe character (default: the tribe's default_model).
messages.cli.tribe.check.option.scenarios: Run every check: the CLI is a fake one that plays the suite's scenarios from ELVARIA_FAKE_SCENARIO.
messages.cli.tribe.check.option.tool: Try another CLI in place of the pinned one (a new version, or a fake one with --scenarios), for this run only: kingdom.json does not change and the tribe is not enabled.
messages.cli.tribe.check.passed_tool: Tribe {tribe} passes the conformance suite with {tool}; kingdom.json is unchanged.
messages.cli.tribe.check.skipped_check: – {check} (skipped: the adapter does not declare it)
messages.cli.tribe.check.summary: Run the conformance suite against a tribe's adapter and check its sign-in; enable the tribe once it passes. Against the real CLI it runs a tiny job, a forbidden push, a kill and a probe, which use a little mana.
messages.cli.tribe.disable.done: Tribe {tribe} is disabled: it takes no new work; its running quests finish, and its quests paused for mana wait (you may reassign them).
messages.cli.tribe.disable.summary: Disable a tribe: no new work; its running quests finish and its paused ones wait. elvaria tribe check enables it again.
messages.cli.tribe.list.broken: adapter file does not load: elvaria tribe check {tribe}
messages.cli.tribe.list.summary: List the tribes: adapter, on or off, pinned CLI and sign-in, the highest rank and guarded territories it may take, what its adapter declares.
messages.cli.tribe.look.also_changed: The drawn look of {tribes} changes with it: the draw walks past the parts other tribes hold.
messages.cli.tribe.look.bad_name: A tribe name is 1 to 24 characters; "{name}" is not.
messages.cli.tribe.look.heading: Tribe {tribe}: {name}, {source}.
messages.cli.tribe.look.how: Change it: elvaria tribe look {tribe} with --palette, --crest, --figure, --aura, --frame <id> or --name <name> (any of them); --reset drops your choice.
messages.cli.tribe.look.no_choice: Tribe {tribe} has no look of your choosing to drop.
messages.cli.tribe.look.no_pool: The kingdom's theme {theme} has no look pool, so its tribes have no look to show.
messages.cli.tribe.look.option.aura: Aura (an id of the theme's pool).
messages.cli.tribe.look.option.crest: Crest (an id of the theme's pool); not another tribe's crest.
messages.cli.tribe.look.option.figure: Figure (an id of the theme's pool).
messages.cli.tribe.look.option.frame: Portrait frame (an id of the theme's pool).
messages.cli.tribe.look.option.name: The tribe's display name, at most 24 characters; without it the name is made of its crest and palette.
messages.cli.tribe.look.option.palette: Palette (an id of the theme's pool); not another tribe's palette.
messages.cli.tribe.look.option.reset: Drop your choice: the tribe takes the theme's pinned look again, or its drawn one.
messages.cli.tribe.look.reset_alone: --reset drops your choice, so it takes no other option.
messages.cli.tribe.look.reset_done: Tribe {tribe}'s chosen look is dropped from kingdom.json.
messages.cli.tribe.look.saved: Tribe {tribe}'s chosen look is written to kingdom.json.
messages.cli.tribe.look.set_aside: kingdom.json chooses parts for tribe {tribe} that the {theme} theme's pool lacks ({parts}): the choice is set aside until it names parts of the pool.
messages.cli.tribe.look.source.generated: drawn from the theme's pool by the tribe id
messages.cli.tribe.look.source.pinned: the theme's own look for it
messages.cli.tribe.look.summary: Show a tribe's look (name, palette, crest, figure, aura, portrait frame) and where it comes from; with options, write your choice to kingdom.json. The look is for display only.
messages.cli.tribe.look.taken: {part} {id} belongs to tribe {other}: the two tribes would look alike. Pick another, or change the look of {other} first.
messages.cli.tribe.look.unknown_part: {part} {id} is not in the look pool of the {theme} theme. The pool has: {ids}.
messages.cli.upgrade.summary: Build a new Elvaria beside the pinned one, try it (migrate, doctor and the conformance suite against fake CLIs on a copy of the kingdom's settings, a script-tier quest on a throwaway kingdom), and only then pin it and run its migrate on the kingdom; --rollback goes back to the build before. 0 mana; refused while a Steward runs.
messages.cli.upgrade.option.ref: Commit, branch or tag of the Elvaria repo this command runs from (default: main).
messages.cli.upgrade.option.rollback: Pin the build before again; nothing is built.
messages.cli.upgrade.no_tool: {program} is not on PATH: elvaria upgrade needs git and pnpm.
messages.cli.upgrade.already: The kingdom already pins build {sha} ({ref}); nothing to do.
messages.cli.upgrade.steward_runs: A Steward, or another upgrade, holds {kingdom}: stop it (Ctrl+C), then run this again.
messages.cli.upgrade.sessions_left: {count} sessions of a stopped Steward still run (elvaria doctor names them). Run elvaria run so it clears them, stop it while no session runs, then upgrade.
messages.cli.upgrade.rollback_sessions: {count} sessions of a stopped Steward still run; the next elvaria run clears them.
messages.cli.upgrade.reusing: Build {sha} ({ref}) is the one before, still at {dir}: it is tried again, not built again.
messages.cli.upgrade.step.prepare: Build: git worktree, pnpm install, hook build
messages.cli.upgrade.step.migrate: Trial: the new build's migrate on a copy of this kingdom's settings
messages.cli.upgrade.step.doctor: Trial: the new build's doctor on that copy
messages.cli.upgrade.step.conformance: Trial: the conformance suite of tribe {tribe} against a fake CLI
messages.cli.upgrade.step.trial: Trial: a script-tier quest on a throwaway kingdom
messages.cli.upgrade.no_fake: – Tribe {tribe}: the build carries no fake CLI for adapter {adapter}, so its conformance suite does not run; elvaria tribe check {tribe} runs it with the tribe's CLI.
messages.cli.upgrade.failed: Not switched: build {sha} failed at step {step}. The kingdom still runs build {current}.
messages.cli.upgrade.failed_first: Not switched: build {sha} failed at step {step}. The kingdom still pins no build.
messages.cli.upgrade.switched: Pinned build {sha}. The build before ({previous}) is kept: elvaria upgrade --rollback goes back to it.
messages.cli.upgrade.switched_first: Pinned build {sha}: from now on every command on this kingdom runs on it.
messages.cli.upgrade.then: Next: elvaria doctor, then elvaria run.
messages.cli.upgrade.migrating: The new build's migrate on the kingdom:
messages.cli.upgrade.migrate_failed: The new build's migrate failed on the kingdom ({reason}), though it passed on the copy. The new build stays pinned: fix the cause and run elvaria migrate, or elvaria upgrade --rollback (the files migrate rewrote have their old text in .backup/).
messages.cli.upgrade.left: Build {sha} stays on disk: {reason}. Remove that folder by hand once no program holds it.
messages.cli.upgrade.no_pointer: The kingdom pins no build: there is nothing to go back from.
messages.cli.upgrade.no_previous: The kingdom has only build {sha}: there is no build before it to go back to.
messages.cli.upgrade.rolled_back: Went back to build {sha}. The build just left ({from}) is kept: elvaria upgrade --ref {full} tries and pins it again.
messages.cli.tribe.unknown: The kingdom has no tribe {tribe}. Tribes: {tribes}.
messages.cli.territory.no_branch: Cannot tell the default branch (detached HEAD, no origin); add --branch <branch>.
messages.cli.territory.none: No territories yet. Add one with: elvaria territory add <folder>
messages.cli.territory.rules_hint: Hint: the repo has {count} files under .claude/rules that Claude Code cannot write; add "{glob}" to laws.patch_paths in territories/{id}/territory.json so characters can change them as a patch.
messages.cli.wake.arg.tribe: The tribe whose account to probe (an id of kingdom.json).
messages.cli.wake.sent: Sent the command to wake tribe {tribe}: the Steward probes its account at its next tick.
messages.cli.wake.summary: Ask the Steward to probe a tribe's mana now, e.g. after signing in again (wake command).
messages.cli.wake.unknown: This kingdom has no tribe {tribe}. Its tribes: {tribes}.
messages.registry.issue.class_kind_mismatch: {where}: classes and quest kinds must list each other.
messages.registry.issue.entry_mismatch: {where}: a script's entry must be scripts/<id>.mjs.
messages.registry.issue.verifier_and_monk: {where}: a class cannot both verify and be a monk.
messages.registry.issue.verifier_takes_work: {where}: a verifier class takes no work (the one who does never judges).
messages.store.issue.exists: {file} exists: this folder is already a kingdom.
messages.store.issue.future_version: {file} was written by a newer Elvaria; left as it is, not read.
messages.store.issue.id_mismatch: {file}: the id inside differs from the file name.
messages.store.issue.locked: {file} is locked by another process; try again later.
messages.store.issue.migration_failed: {file} could not be moved to the current version.
messages.store.issue.missing_version: {file} has no "version" at the top level.
messages.store.issue.not_a_folder: {file} cannot be written: a file stands where its folder must be.
messages.cli.doctor.graph_unpinned: graphify is not pinned: run elvaria doctor --pin, or no quest gets a code graph.
messages.cli.doctor.graph_changed: graphify changed from {pinned} to {version}: check it, then run elvaria doctor --pin.
messages.cli.doctor.graph_no_version: graphify at {path} did not say its version; quests run without a code graph.
messages.cli.doctor.graph_missing: graphify not found: territories {territories} run their quests without a code graph.
messages.cli.doctor.graph_install: Install it with: uv tool install graphifyy (Python 3.10–3.14), then run elvaria doctor --pin.
messages.cli.territory.graph.summary: Build the code graph of a territory at a commit (0 mana) and ask it a question.
messages.cli.territory.graph.option.commit: Commit, branch or tag to build at (default: the tip of the default branch).
messages.cli.territory.graph.option.query: Words to ask the graph (code names and paths work best), as graphify query does.
messages.cli.territory.graph.built: Built the code graph of {territory} at {commit}: {nodes} nodes, {edges} edges, {seconds} s, in {dir}.
messages.cli.territory.graph.reused: The code graph of {territory} at {commit} is built already, in {dir}.
messages.cli.territory.graph.unknown: There is no territory {id}; see elvaria territory list.
messages.cli.territory.graph.no_git: Territory {id} has no git: a code graph is built at a commit.
messages.cli.territory.graph.no_graphify: No graphify is pinned (or git is missing): install graphify and run elvaria doctor --pin.
messages.cli.territory.graph.no_commit: git does not know {ref} in this territory.
messages.cli.territory.check.summary: Scores a territory: tries commands.setup and every check on a clean plot at the head of its default branch, then prints its scorecard (0 mana).
messages.cli.territory.check.unknown: No territory {id}; see elvaria territory list.
messages.cli.territory.check.trying: Trying territory {id}: a clean plot at the head of {branch}, commands.setup then every check, as the Steward runs them (this may take minutes)…
messages.cli.territory.check.stopped: Trial stopped; its plot is gone and no result was kept.
messages.cli.territory.check.leftover: The trial's folder stays: {detail}. Close the program holding it; the next trial removes it first.
messages.cli.territory.check.title: Scorecard of territory {id}, tried on {branch} ({base}):
messages.cli.territory.check.ready: Ready: the trial passes; {count} other items do not, see docs/guides/operating-a-kingdom.md §3 for the fixes.
messages.cli.territory.check.not_ready: Not ready: the trial fails. Fix it, then run elvaria territory check {id} again.
messages.cli.territory.check.untried: Territory {id} has no git, so nothing was tried; the other items stand as above.
messages.cli.territory.check.item.trial: Trial: setup and every check on a clean plot of the default branch
messages.cli.territory.check.item.set_aside: Runs of checks set aside for their environment
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.no_git: The territory has no git: there is no default branch to try.
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.plot_failed: No plot could be made for the trial: {detail}
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.setup_failed: commands.setup failed: {command} (exit code {exit}). First error line: {line} Log: {log}
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.setup_environ: commands.setup failed because of its environment: {command}. Line: {line} Log: {log}
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.no_checks: The territory has no checks: only the judge reads the work of its quests.
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.check_failed: Check {check} fails on the default branch: {command} (exit code {exit}). First error line: {line} Log: {log}
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.check_timed_o: Check {check} timed out on the default branch: {command}. Log: {log}
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.check_environ: Check {check} failed because of its environment: {command}. Line: {line} Log: {log}
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.check_slow: {check}: {seconds} s, over {max} % of its {minutes} min timeout: on a busy machine it is cut. Raise timeout_minutes or make the check faster.
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.few_check_run: The territory has {runs} runs of checks so far, {min} at least to measure.
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.set_aside_rat: {set_aside}/{runs} runs of checks set aside for their environment ({rate} %, at most {max} %).
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.gazetteer_mis: No gazetteer (territories/<id>/gazetteer.md), or it is empty.
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.gazetteer_uns: The gazetteer has no <!-- elvaria:commit <sha> --> stamp on its first line: nobody knows whether it is fresh.
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.gazetteer_sta: The gazetteer was written at {stamp}; the commits since were not counted.
git does not know the commit {stamp} of the gazetteer's stamp.
The gazetteer was written at {stamp}, {commits} commits ago (at most {max}): read it again, fix it, and stamp the new commit.
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.gazetteer_fre: The gazetteer was written at {stamp}, {commits} commits ago.
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.gazetteer_nam: The gazetteer names all {count} of the territory's commands.
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.shared_paths_: shared_paths not declared; with no hot files, declare an empty list.
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.protected_pat: laws.protected_paths not declared; with nothing to guard, declare an empty list.
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.few_decided: The territory has {decided} quests whose first run was decided, {min} at least to measure.
messages.cli.territory.check.reason.first_pass_ra: {passed}/{decided} quests passed their first run ({rate} %, at least {min} %).
messages.cli.doctor.trial_none: Territory {id} was never tried: run elvaria territory check {id} before its first quest.
messages.cli.doctor.trial_unreadable: The last trial of territory {id} cannot be read ({file}); run elvaria territory check {id} again.
messages.cli.doctor.trial_failed: Territory {id} failed its trial at {at}; fix it, then run elvaria territory check {id} again.
messages.cli.doctor.trial_stale: Territory {id}'s commands.setup or checks changed since its trial at {at}; run elvaria territory check {id} again.
messages.cli.doctor.trial_passed_gaps: Territory {id}: passed its trial at {at}; {count} other items of its scorecard do not (elvaria territory check {id}).
messages.tribe_look.name: {palette} {crest}
